ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The quarter’s missed volume is primarily budget-limited across the scaling campaigns (most are at ~99.9% budget utilization with 78–83% impression share lost to budget), not a systemic rank/quality issue at the campaign level (impression share lost to rank is 0% in every campaign). There is, however, a separate rank issue at the keyword level (several high-QS terms still show 79–81% lost to rank), plus measurable efficiency leakage from competitor-brand zero-click queries (2,058 impressions; 56.1% of search-term impressions from those terms) and a small but real self-inflicted block from negative conflicts (6,940 estimated impressions blocked) inside the main non-brand search campaign.
notable_patterns: Shopping and growth campaigns are consistently capped: Shopping - Apparel (18% search impression share; 82% lost to budget; 99.9% budget utilization), Shopping - Electronics (17% IS; 83% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization), Shopping - Home & Garden (19% IS; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization), Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo (21% IS; 79% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization), and Performance Max - Full Catalog (19% IS; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization).

Brand Search is the exception: 75.4% budget utilization yet still 40% impression share lost to budget (60% IS), indicating the brand campaign likely needs a higher budget cap despite not “hitting” budget every day (e.g., dayparting/spikes or shared budget dynamics).

Keyword-level rank pressure exists even when QS is strong: “holiday electronics deals” (QS 7.5) has only 19% impression share with 81% lost to rank; “winter jacket sale” (QS 8.0) has 21% IS with 79% lost to rank. This suggests bid/auction pressure on high-intent terms even though campaign-level lost-to-rank is 0%.

Competitor leakage is substantial and unproductive: 2,058 competitor-brand zero-click impressions, with no competitor-brand terms that convert; those zero-click competitor terms make up 56.1% of search-term impressions in the extracted set (e.g., “delphi retail group”, “marathon mercantile”, “ionian goods co”, “acropolis retail quote”).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Demand is being throttled by budget: only 18% impression share while 82% is lost to budget at 99.9% budget utilization. ROAS is 3.33 on €541.50 spend, so there’s room to scale if margin targets allow.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget (or reallocate from lower-priority areas) and pair with product-level pruning (exclude/limit low-ROAS SKUs) to scale impression share without diluting ROAS.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Severely budget-capped (17% impression share; 83% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization). With ROAS 3.29 on €347.90, incremental budget should be tested, but electronics is also where high-intent keywords show heavy rank loss (e.g., “holiday electronics deals” 81% lost to rank).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget and simultaneously raise bids/targets on the highest-intent electronics segments (or split them into a higher-priority structure) to reduce rank loss on proven deal-intent traffic.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Budget is the binding constraint (19% impression share; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization). ROAS is comparatively stronger at 4.34 on €382.90, making it a good candidate to receive incremental budget first.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize budget increases here ahead of lower-ROAS capped campaigns to capture additional volume at similar efficiency.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Heavily constrained by budget (21% impression share; 79% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) and also impacted by account-level negatives blocking live intent (6,940 estimated impressions blocked across 3 conflicts within this campaign). QS is strong (avg 8.8), so unlocking volume should be primarily a budget + traffic-shaping exercise.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget while cleaning negative conflicts and tightening query intent (especially excluding competitor-brand terms that generate zero clicks and no conversions).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Meaningfully budget-limited (19% impression share; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization). ROAS is 4.91 on €98.70, suggesting incremental spend is likely to be efficient if feed hygiene/asset coverage remains strong.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Scale budget in controlled steps and confirm product coverage/segmentation so additional spend concentrates on higher-return categories.

recommendation_cards.title: Raise budgets on the capped campaigns (start with Home & Garden + PMax) to capture the 78–83% budget-lost impression share
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Five core scaling campaigns are effectively maxed out (99.9% budget utilization) while losing most auctions to budget: Shopping - Apparel (82% lost to budget; 18% IS), Shopping - Electronics (83%; 17% IS), Shopping - Home & Garden (81%; 19% IS), Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo (79%; 21% IS), and Performance Max - Full Catalog (81%; 19% IS). Home & Garden also has the strongest ROAS among the large Shopping campaigns at 4.34 (vs Apparel 3.33; Electronics 3.29), and PMax is at 4.91 ROAS.
recommended_steps: Increase daily budgets in 15–25% steps for Shopping - Home & Garden and Performance Max - Full Catalog first; reassess after 5–7 days before the next step.
If total budget is fixed, reallocate from the lowest-return capped areas (e.g., shift incremental budget away from Shopping - Electronics (3.29 ROAS) toward Home & Garden (4.34) and PMax (4.91)).
Set a guardrail target (e.g., maintain ROAS within ~10% of current levels) while scaling, rather than scaling all capped campaigns equally.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share lost to budget in the scaled campaigns (target: reduce from ~79–83% down toward <60% initially) alongside ROAS stability (keep Home & Garden near ~4.3+; PMax near ~4.9+).

recommendation_cards.title: Fix self-blocking negatives in Non-Brand Search to recover ~6,940 blocked impressions (then decide what to actually exclude)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 3 conflicts blocking an estimated 6,940 impressions inside Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo: negative “free” blocks the keyword “free shipping promo code” (5,200 blocked imps), “DIY” blocks “kitchen appliances clearance DIY install” (980), and “returns” blocks “winter jacket sale returns policy” (760). At the same time, “free shipping promo code” is also a low-QS/high-cost term (QS 3.5; €24.18 spend; €60.45 cost/conv), so the fix should be intentional rather than simply ‘unblocking everything’.
recommended_steps: Remove or narrow the negatives causing unintended blocks (e.g., move from broad negatives to more specific phrase/exact negatives, or apply them to a different scope) so the campaign’s keyword strategy matches its negative strategy.

After unblocking, immediately separate intent: keep “returns policy” traffic in a dedicated ad group (or exclude it intentionally if it’s customer-service oriented), and decide whether “free shipping promo code” belongs at all given QS 3.5 and €60.45 cost/conv.
Re-check the conflicts report after changes to confirm blocked impressions drop materially from 6,940.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Blocked impressions from negative conflicts (target: near-zero conflicts; recover a meaningful portion of the 6,940 blocked imps) and cost/conv on any newly unblocked segments (keep below current problem levels like €60+).

recommendation_cards.title: Exclude competitor-brand queries that generate 2,058 zero-click impressions and zero conversions
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Search-term evidence shows 2,058 competitor-brand zero-click impressions and no competitor-brand terms that convert; 56.1% of the search-term impressions in the extracted set come from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., “delphi retail group”, “marathon mercantile”, “ionian goods co”, “acropolis retail quote”). This is pure auction participation without engagement, which can also crowd out budget in already budget-capped campaigns (e.g., Non-Brand Search at 99.9% utilization).
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand names (and common variants) as negatives in non-brand search and any campaign types where you’re not explicitly running conquesting with dedicated ads/landing pages.
Create an exception list only if you choose to run a controlled competitor strategy later (separate budget + tailored messaging); otherwise keep exclusions tight and comprehensive.
Re-audit the search-terms list after 7–14 days to ensure competitor-brand impression volume and spend approach zero.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Competitor-brand impressions and clicks (target: competitor-brand clicks remain ~0 and impressions drop materially from 2,058), plus overall non-brand CPA/ROAS improvement after removing wasted auctions.

recommendation_cards.title: Address rank loss on high-intent, high-QS keywords by raising bids or isolating them into a premium segment
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Despite good quality scores, some high-intent terms are losing most impressions to rank: “holiday electronics deals” (QS 7.5) has 19% impression share with 81% lost to rank; “winter jacket sale” (QS 8.0) has 21% IS with 79% lost to rank; even “pilot account promo code” (QS 9.5) shows 42% lost to rank with 58% IS. This is consistent with auction pressure rather than relevance issues, and it’s separate from the campaign-level lost-to-rank=0% pattern.
recommended_steps: Isolate these terms into their own ad groups (or a dedicated campaign) with higher bids/targets so they don’t compete with broader, lower-intent traffic for rank.
Apply bid uplifts specifically to these queries/terms first (not across the board), then reassess lost-to-rank after a week.
If budget is still the limiter after bid changes, prioritize incremental budget to the segments where rank improvements are producing incremental conversions efficiently.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share lost to rank on these exact terms (target: reduce “holiday electronics deals” lost-to-rank from 81% to <60% initially; similar for “winter jacket sale” from 79% to <60%) while monitoring cost/conv for deterioration.

recommendation_cards.title: Trim or fence off low-QS, high-cost keywords before scaling budgets further
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Several low-quality keywords are consuming spend inefficiently: “free shipping promo code” (QS 3.5; €24.18 spend; €60.45 cost/conv), “deals near me today” (QS 2.5; €15.39 spend; no recorded conversions), and “kitchen appliances clearance” (QS 3.0; €9.60 spend; €96.00 cost/conv). Keyword-level stats also suggest higher QS tends to associate with lower cost/conv (r = -0.771), so reducing exposure to QS 2.5–3.5 traffic should help efficiency as you add budget.
recommended_steps: Pause or reduce bids on the worst performers immediately (“deals near me today”; “kitchen appliances clearance”) and move any remaining broad ‘promo code’ traffic into a tightly controlled ad group with stricter query negatives.
Rewrite/realign ads and landing pages only for the terms you keep, aiming to lift QS from ~3 to 5+; otherwise, don’t fund them while budget is tight.
Reallocate freed spend toward the higher-intent segments where you’re currently losing impression share to budget (79–83%) or rank (79–81% on the noted terms).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Spend share on QS ≤3.5 terms (target: down materially) and account cost/conv stability while budgets rise.

already_working: Ad assets are not the bottleneck: 100% of ads are rated Good or Excellent (4 Excellent, 4 Good), so performance lifts should come more from budget/query/bid changes than wholesale ad rewrites.

Auction presence versus named competitors is generally competitive (avg outranking share 52.9%; avg top-of-page rate self 49.6% vs competitor 42.4%), supporting that the big headroom is impression volume (budget caps) rather than being consistently outclassed in position.
Brand Search efficiency is strong (ROAS 24.26 on €494.34 with 121.2 conversions), so scaling brand coverage (if demand exists) is low risk compared to non-brand expansion.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: You’re currently under-capturing demand primarily because budget caps are throttling auction participation (78.7% of impressions lost to budget) while the broader retail search market is simultaneously getting more competitive in your market (Greece retail search spend +9.0% QoQ). With your impression share (21.29%) already well below the retail benchmark (35.0%), waiting risks ceding incremental impression share to competitors who are increasing spend, making future catch-up more expensive. Acting now is most justified in areas where you can immediately buy back lost reach (budget-limited campaigns) and stop obvious waste (negative conflicts / competitor zero-click queries), then selectively defend high-intent terms that are facing auction pressure.

email_copy.subject: EUR 12,644 sitting behind a 78.7% budget cap in your paid search
email_copy.hook: Your paid search account isn’t being held back by ad strength or broad “ranking issues” — it’s mostly being throttled by budget caps in the campaigns that should be doing the scaling work (many are effectively maxed out). The result is you’re showing up for a fraction of the demand you’re already eligible to win.
why_now_bullets: Market benchmark IS is 35.0%; your account is at 21.29% — you’re under-present right as auctions get tighter.
In Greece retail search, spend is up +9.0% QoQ while your account is losing 78.7% of impressions to budget — competitors are leaning in as you’re being forced out of auctions.
Your campaign-level lost-to-rank is 0.0%, but you’re still missing volume because budgets are the limiter — the fastest wins here are “buy back reach” moves, not a long relevance rebuild.
email_copy.stat_sub: Created by removing budget throttles + cutting obvious query waste
email_copy.impact_line: We sized EUR 12,644 in incremental revenue available this quarter by first unlocking the campaigns that are hitting the ceiling, then stopping two avoidable leaks (self-blocking negatives and competitor-brand zero-click participation). With a daily budget of EUR 420, this is less about “doing more work” and more about redirecting spend toward the auctions that actually produce incremental sales.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is the campaign-by-campaign breakout of where that EUR 12,644 is being left on the table today (and where it comes back fastest).
email_copy.cards_intro: Here’s the prioritized fix list — designed to (1) remove the hard caps, (2) eliminate waste that’s stealing budget from real buyers, and (3) selectively pay for rank only where intent is proven.
email_copy.working_intro: Also calling out what’s already solid in the account so we don’t touch what isn’t broken.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If you want a simple goalpost: moving from 21.29% impression share toward 35.0% is what drives the payoff — the extra reach is where the incremental EUR 12,644 comes from, without needing to reinvent your creative.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map the 15-minute rollout plan?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with “Tue” or “Thu” and I’ll send two specific time slots. If you’d rather keep it async, reply “plan” and I’ll send the exact sequence of changes to make first (with the guardrails to watch).
email_copy.ps: One quick reassurance: because campaign-level lost-to-rank is 0.0%, this is primarily a budget-availability and query-shaping problem — meaning you can see movement quickly once the caps and leaks are addressed.
